description:
baselines/perl-suite-run.tsv says op/coreamp.t is 9 ok / 58 not-ok, measured at
s488a.  s495 measured 10/57 on the s492c tree AND 10/57 on a 5ce155cb
extraction of main -- so the move is PRE-EXISTING and unattributed; nothing in
s492c touched it (probed: the `&uc` and `&uc with too many args` rows are
"(missing)" on both sides, byte for byte).

The row-level churn it reports (NEW `&uc`, FIXED `&bless in list context`) is
the 500-row LOG CAP the snapshot's own note already warns about: the file logs
501 of its 778 rows, so two rows leave the log as two enter it whenever the
file's row count shifts.

WHAT THIS NEEDS: a bisect of the range s488a..5ce155cb for the one row, or a
decision to re-bless the row with "cap artifact" as the cause.  It is NOT a
regression and it is not worth a batch on its own -- it is here so the next
session that sees op/coreamp.t as a "mover" can stop in one grep.
subject: The op/coreamp.t snapshot row is STALE: 9/58 blessed, 10/57 measured on BOTH the base and the tree (s495)
